intended_object: The canonical chain null-homotopy of i_* ∘ (id − φ_*) on singular chains: i is the inclusion of the fibre F into the mapping torus of φ, and φ_* is the map φ induces on chains. It is obtained from the cylinder homotopy between i∘φ and i and is used to build the mapping-cone map underlying the Wang sequence (inferred from the docstring, the module doc citing Hatcher §2.2, and its use in wangMappingConeMap).
explanation: The body takes `singularChainHomotopy`, a homotopy from φ_* ≫ i_* to i_* induced by the cylinder homotopy through Mathlib's homotopy invariance of singular chains. It reverses it with `.symm`, turns it into a homotopy from i_* − φ_* ≫ i_* to 0 with `Homotopy.equivSubZero`, and uses `Homotopy.ofEq` to rewrite (𝟙 − φ_*) ≫ i_* as i_* − φ_* ≫ i_*. The result is a correct null-homotopy of `wangEndomorphism ≫ fibreInclusionChainMap`. Its components are minus those of the canonical homotopy (lemma `wangNullHomotopy_hom`), which matches the sign convention in the docstring. The coefficients are fully general: any preadditive category with coproducts and any object R; F is any topological space and φ any homeomorphism. Mathlib has no mapping-torus or Wang-sequence construction, so there is no more general counterpart. The definition is a fairly auxiliary datum feeding `wangMappingConeMap`, so `not_a_mathematical_object` would also be defensible, but it is a precise chain homotopy from the standard derivation of the Wang sequence, and it is constructed correctly.
